rationale: Set A wins because it separates four real protagonists - investor, merchandising strategy, materials, and channel - and gives each one the proof burden it would need before a reporter bites. Its "Allbirds posts its first gross-margin improvement as the turnaround plan starts to bite" is a legitimate public-company turnaround story; B takes "Can one good quarter win back investors holding Allbirds below its IPO price?" and calls it "duplicate," which is how you throw away the desk most likely to care about a public, unprofitable stock. B's "Allbirds' comeback runs through someone else's shelves" is usable, but the set compresses too much of the finance story into retail operations and loses a real angle.
gaps_in_A: "Story type: funding-mechanics" is the wrong label for a public-company margin/turnaround story. It is markets or retail earnings, not funding mechanics.
"The prevailing belief in DTC retail is that growth comes from expanding the range and the store footprint" is a smart hypothesis, but it is not in the update. Pitch it as a test, not a fact.
"durability is the chronic knock against natural-material shoes" adds outside context not supplied. It may be true, but this judge only gets the update.
"as the turnaround plan starts to bite" leans causal before the set has the causal breakdown it correctly says it needs.
gaps_in_B: "Can one good quarter win back investors holding Allbirds below its IPO price?" marked as "duplicate" is the biggest miss. That is a distinct markets/equity story, not just a weaker version of the retail operations angle.

"store closures plus a 40% product-range cut producing the first quarter of gross-margin improvement" overclaims causality. The update says margin improved under the plan, not which action produced it.
"making a wholesale partnership a centerpiece of its relaunch" invents hierarchy. The update says a named wholesale partnership is part of the relaunch, not the centerpiece.
"A retail-business reporter at a retail or DTC trade outlet" misses the financial outlet or markets reporter that the public, unprofitable, below-IPO-price facts clearly tee up.
